input.description: Check class definition lines for Client hierarchy

toolu_1ba96af4d5d2322a04bc5af3.description: Check class definition lines for Client hierarchy

content.text:
All three live in `httpx/_client.py`:

- **`BaseClient`** (`httpx/_client.py:188`) — the shared base class holding sync/async-agnostic state and logic: cookies, headers, params, base_url, auth, event hooks, timeout/proxy config, redirect handling, URL/header/cookie/query merging (`_merge_url`, `_merge_cookies`, `_merge_headers`, `_merge_queryparams`), and redirect-request building (`_build_redirect_request`, `_redirect_url`, `_redirect_method`, `_redirect_headers`).
- **`Client(BaseClient)`** (`httpx/_client.py:594`) — the synchronous client. Adds blocking I/O methods: `.send()`, `.request()`, `.stream()`, the verb shortcuts (`.get()`, `.post()`, `.put()`, `.patch()`, `.delete()`, `.head()`, `.options()`), `._send_single_request()`, `._send_handling_auth()`, `._send_handling_redirects()`, `._transport_for_url()`, `.close()`, `__enter__`/`__exit__`.
- **`AsyncClient(BaseClient)`** (`httpx/_client.py:1307`) — the async counterpart, mirroring `Client`'s API as coroutines (`async def .send()`, `.request()`, `.stream()`, verb methods, `._send_single_request`, etc.) plus `.aclose()`, `__aenter__`/`__aexit__`.

So `Client` and `AsyncClient` are siblings, both inheriting from `BaseClient`, which centralizes configuration/state and URL/request-merging logic, while each subclass implements the actual request-sending transport logic for its sync/async execution model respectively.
